Press Release:


Follow the Guns


In an extraordinary investigation arms trafficking investigator Kathi Lynn Austin races against time to expose the suppliers and manufacturers of guns and bullets recovered at rhino poaching crime scenes.


Carte Blanche joins forces with Austin, a United Nations arms expert who has founded the Conflict Awareness Project, to reveal the origin of weapons confiscated along the Kruger National Park border fence with Mozambique. We trace the owners of businesses who make their living from facilitating the movement of guns from Europe to Southern Africa.


Anti-poaching initiatives consume growing resources with diminishing returns as two or more rhinos are slaughtered for their horns every day and gram for gram rhino horn remains the world’s most lucrative substance.


Carte Blanche reveals how the militarisation of the fight against poachers themselves has yielded little fruit amid a never-ending supply of guns and we set our sights on a new target – the dedicated gun supply chains that arm the poachers.


PRODUCER: Sasha Schwendenwein & Kathi Lynn Austin
PRESENTER: Kathi Lynn Austin

Script:


SECTION 1
Over the past six years, South Africa has ...waged a bloody WAR against rhino poaching.
Soundup: JJ: “We were involved last year in almost 100 firefights, 2 firefights a week.”

The results of this 24.7 battle? Millions spent by well-intentioned celebrities and donors, hundreds of impoverished poachers killed, rangers lives torn apart, and still - 1 rhino is killed every 8 hours.
JJ: “It’s low risk and high return. This is almost a poacher’s supermarket.”

With over 7,200 rhinos butchered to date, and no end in sight to the horrific carnage, this prehistoric species could be extinct within a decade. Clearly those fighting to protect rhinos must re-think who the enemy is. And my investigation shows the worst criminals are not the ordinary poachers, but the shadowy kingpins behind them.

Join me on my journey and discover some of the masterminds orchestrating the mass slaughter of rhinos.
SOUNDUP CNN: “KATHI LYNN AUSTIN HAS SPENT THE PAST… AND THE BIG QUESTION IS WHOSE NEXT?

I have found the key to unlocking this deadly mystery. And that key is to Follow The Guns. As an independent arms trafficking investigator, I do not work for any government or agency, rather funding comes through the NGO – the Conflict Awareness Project. In late 2014 rhinos were dying in Kruger National Park in even greater numbers even though the park had acquired a whole new arsenal of weapons. Conservation groups had begun to feel like they were funding an arms race, so they asked me to assess the situation. I headed to ground zero. Kruger National Park is the world’s biggest rhino sanctuary. And it’s a VAST nature reserve that borders Mozambique, a well-known smugglers’ hub.
SOUND OF CRUNCH on Veld – walking
LINK: “WE’RE WALKING OUT TO A CRIME SCENE WHERE THERE’S A 3 DAY OLD RHINO CARCASS.
UPSOUND: “Cutting into carcass”
LINK: we have the crime scene investigator Frikkie. he’s been looking for bullets inside the torso of the rhino
Kathi: What kind of weapons do you usually see?
Frikkie: Well now a days is more heavy caliber, like this for example. It’s a fairly high powered rifle, as well as other .375, and .458 is the most popular type of weapon. a
Kathi: Are you able to trace those weapons back?
Frikkie: “It will be one of the plus points if we can trace it back to the original owner. Then the Mozambican government can do something about these people.” Kathi: “We’ll get those bastards. I promise you.”
Army General Johan Jooste left a job as a top-level weapons salesman to head up anti-poaching in the Kruger. So I expected his team to focus on the enemies’ rifles. But Jooste’s militarized approach kicks in only after poachers are spotted or a rhino is slain.
VO: 25 YEARS OF INVESTIGATING GUNS TELLS ME KRUGER’S ANTI-POACHING FORCES SHOULD TREAT EACH RHINO MURDER AS COMPLEX SERIAL CRIME SCENE. ADD UP ALL THE GUN EVIDENCE, ACT ON THAT, AND IT WILL LEAD US TO THE BIG PLAYERS.
All good crime investigators know that to find a culprit, you must figure out their motive, opportunity and means. The motive here is simple math. A pair of horns can fetch up to 20 million rand.
Johan Jooste: Gram for Gram, Rhino horn right now, is the most expensive commodity on the planet.”
The opportunity is also easy to spot: corruption and an inexhaustible supply of poachers makes rhinos an easy target. But only after I examined the means did I formulate a working hypothesis: industrial level poaching did not take off until the kingpins had set up their own gun supply chain. To start piecing together this weapons puzzle, I needed allies within the counter poaching community so I could see how the guns were being used.
This broken fence is the border between the Kruger National Park and Mozambique – the frontline where the rangers encounter the poachers.
UPSOUND: Kathi: You can tell that’s fresh because?
Ranger: You can see the grass hasn’t come up yet and been disturbed it here.
UPSOUND: Ranger: Poachers like to sit at the water points. so we always just keep it down.
The expert trackers spot vultures - an ominous sign. Ranger: pointing.
Later we learn 3 rhino carcasses were found a few kilometers away inside Kruger Park.
Along a path travelled by poachers I find an unexpected clue – newly discarded boxes from a hunting rifle. It’s a brand manufactured in the Czech Republic commonly referred to as CZ. I quickly ask to see the rangers incidents reports on poaching.
LINK: SO HERE, THIS INCIDENT RECORDS WHAT FIREARM THEY HAD IN THEIR POSSESSION. I CAN JUST SEE RIGHT HERE. CZ CZ, THIS IS THE WAY THAT I FOUND MY PATTERN, ALMOST ALL OF THE WEAPONS SINCE END OF 2012 ARE ALMOST ALL CZECH MANUFACTURED, AND SEE THE SERIAL NUMBERS AS BEING EXPORTED SOME FROM THE US.
The bullets used, the fresh CZ boxes, a single brand, all point to the CZ gun manufacturer as the supplier of choice. It’s used to pierce the thick skin of a rhino in a single shot.
Alex: These Czech made firearms are cheaper than a lot of the other firearms, that’s why they’re coming into the system.
Alex McDonald manages the Mozambican private reserve where the poachers’ CZ guns were recovered. He confirms a wider conspiracy.
Alex: Maybe these guns are being imported not just from the Czech republic but from the US. The answer comes from higher up the levels, finding out where the guns are coming from, who’s doing the transporting, where are they being kept? Unfortunately guys that are investigating that, arresting those people are involved themselves.
When it comes to the involvement of the big players, the weapons are far more valuable than the poachers’ lives.
Alex: If they return home without a rifle, they are close to being dead. That, next to the rhino horn, is the second most important thing up the chain.
I see it the other way around. Without the guns there can be no horn. Either way, you’ve heard the expression follow the money? The problem is you can’t. Rhino horn is a cash-traded commodity. But guns? They do leave a paper trail and that starts with a serial number. Since anti-poaching forces have not systematized the gun evidence, I’ll need to create my own serial number database and use that to hone in on the big fish.
I visit gun shops, anti-poaching units, police offices, and the Kruger’s gunsmith.
Fritz: “This is the model specifically made for the American market which is upper class...
Kathi: Is that the Safari Classic?
Fritz: Yes. That is actually something we should take back to the American dealers and explain how these rifles end up here.”
But my real treasure trove is in the police vaults where all the recovered weapons are stored.
SOUNDUP: Unlocking of door. Kathi: And the serial number is very clear on here. Policeman: It’s interesting that it is a CZ 550 magnum.

VO: I DISCOVER THAT THE SERIAL NUMBERS RUN CLOSE TOGETHER, WHICH MEANS THEY COME FROM THE SAME SHIPMENTS. THAT PROVES THE RHINO SYNDICATE HAD ESTABLISHED A DEDICATED GUN SUPPLY CHAIN. THIS IS HOW THEY WERE ABLE TO KILL SO MANY RHINOS IN SUCH A SHORT TIME AND DRAMATICALLY INCREASE THE MARKET DEMAND.

K: I know that you have confiscated some CZ’s that are also made in the US, they have a double stamp. Normally they start with a serial number A. What does that start with?
Policeman: A.
K: That’s an A!
To track and trace the serial numbers I’ve collected I must start at the top of the weapons pipeline - the gun manufacturer in the Czech Republic. Afterwards, I’ll work each step down all the way to the rhino murder scenes. I travel to a provincial Czech town where the gun factory is located.
UPSOUND: WALKING IN
I rely on my international reputation to get my foot in the door...I give CZ samples of the serial numbers of Kruger’s recovered guns. And at first, they seem willing to assist.
LINK: THIS INFO WILL HELP ME IDENTIFY WHO THE ARMS TRAFFICKERS ARE, AND WHOSE CONNECTED TO RHINO POACHING SYNDICATES.
A shocking pattern is revealed: two clients bought nearly all of the CZ rifles, ExploAfrica and Fabitrade which trades as Casa Fabiao. This doesn’t look good, so CZ invite me to the largest annual hunting exhibition in Germany called IWA, where they’ll arrange for me to question their clients. I’ll also get to discuss the incriminating data with CZ’s head of Africa sales, Petr Kallus. You need to record every move in the murky world of black market arms deals, so I get myself a hidden camera. But when I get to the gun show, CZ repeatedly obstructs, changing the clients’ meeting times on me. UPSOUND: He’s here in germany, and im in germany trying to meet him.”
So, I search for the gun dealers myself - but in vain. I then pin down Petr Kallus who claims his clients told him their guns were stolen. SOUNDUP: Petr Kallus: “We’ll try to find out the information which will either say to us the guns have been stolen in mozam, and it means that the partner is not involved.”
CZ and their clients can no longer deny knowledge that their guns are used in poaching crimes. This is important - as it may be used against them later in a court of law. But I still need Kallus on the record, which he concedes to back at factory headquarters.
Petr Kallus: We do never do the business which we are not allowed to do. According to the serial number, which is on every gun, we can track every customer to whom we are selling these guns, and we know that most of the weapons which er have been found in the Kruger Park, were sold to Mozambique. We are not a part of er of this er of this um way from the – from our client to, to the poacher.
Finally, after all the games, answers.
Petr Kallus: There are two clients in Mozambique, this is ninety percent, maybe ninety-five percent of the serial numbers you, you gave me…

VO: WHAT HE SAID NEXT MADE ME QUESTION CZ’S MOTIVE. WHY RISK THEIR ENTIRE INTERNATIONAL REPUTATION FOR A TINY MARKET LIKE MOZAMBIQUE?
Petr: We can say it’s 1.01% of our business, so it’s not so significant for us. Kathi: Is there a difference between the licensing products with military grade weapons and hunting rifles?
Petr Kallus: “Military weapons are more strict. With the hunting business, those weapons are not considered so dangerous for, uh, for using against the people.”
Perhaps in another era, but these guns now play a major part in violent organized crime.
I leave my dossier with the Czech Republic prosecutor and the wildlife crime authorities who respond by opening a case. None of us believe that the guns coming from the Czech Republic is a mere coincidence. An Interpol report shows the country hosts one of the largest Vietnamese communities in Europe, a proven hub for the smuggling of rhino horn. The next stop on the gun supply chain is CZ’s two clients in Mozambique. Armed with their names and documents, I am confident my evidence file is taking shape.

SECTION 2


My suspicions about the CZ gun maker’s role in supplying guns to the rhino syndicates only increases, when they don’t halt shipments to their two Mozambican clients - ExploAfrica and Casa Fabiao. Astounded, I also learned a new CZ gun consignment will soon make its way to ExploAfrica.
The world needs to wake up to the fact that hunting rifles are the tools of dangerous criminals - and they’re less regulated than military weapons. As if to placate me, CZ sends a parting email with the most damning clue yet. A list of gun buyers from their Mozambican client Casa Fabiao, revealing that one company - INVESTCON - bought almost their entire hunting rifle stock. A new target to add to my list.
My first stop is the larger of the two importers of CZ hunting rifles. This takes me to rural Matola, near Mozambique’s capital Maputo. ExploAfrica is a giant explosives company.With their impending arms shipment, I need to speak to their big boss - Miguel Vieira. After several days tracking him, I finally catch him and his deputy Manuel.
Kathi: South Africa is saying some of these weapons are going to the wrong people. Because, there’s is a shipment that is coming...

Vieira deflects saying the owners are in Portugal.
Roberto: Exploafrica is based here in Mozambique. The main company that owns exploafrica is a portuguese company.

LINK: IT’S A PORTUGUESE COMPANY, WHICH IS EXACTLY WHAT CZ WAS SAYING IT WAS NOT. BECAUSE IT’S ILLEGAL FOR THEM TO RE-EXPORT TO MOZAMBIQUE AND SO THAT’S BASICALLY WHAT THEY'RE DOING, SO THE PLOT THICKENS....

Since the sales are going through Portugal, the Mozambican licenses appear to be violated by CZ. I must now factor in the Portuguese step of the gun supply chain. But first I want to expose all the local players, and to do that, I need ExploAfrica’s gun records. Miguel Vieira told me they’re stored at their Maputo gun-shop - Afrocaça. The manager is Dercio Daude.

Kathi: Okay.

I tell him I know he’s ordered a new shipment of guns from CZ.
Upsound: Kathi: CZ, is still, they said it might take two months?
Dercio: Yes, yes, yes.

Dercio: Yes that’s correct.

Dercio: Investcon is game farm.

Dercio: Yes I know them. Some guys from south Africa.

KATHI LINK: THESE GUYS ARE BUYING FROM BOTH COMPANIES. THE QUANTITIES IS VERY HIGH. SO I THINK INVESTCON IS OUR TARGET.

While we look over Afrocaca’s gun purchases, I find a serial number linking Investcon directly to a gun recovered from a Kruger rhino crime scene.

Kathi: It’s investcon. Yeah that’s it! Because on the south African side, they have found this weapon.

Dercio gives me the contact details for Investcon’s owner.
Dercio: This guy is the owner of Vaquita guest house. The name is Johan. The authorization to buy maybe 16 weapons.
Kathi: So now?
Dercio: Yes.
Kathi: So they have a new order?
Dercio: Yes.
I need to unmask Investcon, so I get ownership certificates from Mozambique’s public records and conduct a web search using special software. I find out that Johan is the professional hunter Johan Stoltz, and Investcon trades as a game farm called Limnetzi Safaris. I also learn his base of operations is Vaquita guest house. I decide it’s now time to go there and have a drink.
Kathi: What is your connection to Investcon?
Johan: Investcon is myself and my dad, and er 1 of the guys in the government, but he’s a ex-governor of Gaza [province]. But, er, that company I’m not really using that – more the safari company at this stage.
I asked Stoltz about the illegal gun business he answers hypothetically, baiting me.
Johan: I contact CZ. Say listen I want to buy 5 guns, 5 rifles. What do you require from me? Money? Shoop! I transfer money. Send me my rifles.
Kathi: Right.
*White flash
I can get rifles into Mozambique, plenty. No licenses, no nothing. And I can sell them. No paperwork. Plenty. (flash)
And those rifles. those guys who is hunting rhino, that’s how they get their hands on those rifles.
Cops come, they chuck it – they're getting a million rand a, a horn. Who worries about twenty thousand fucking rand, for a rifle? Just get another one.
(flash)
Money makes things that is bent, straight here. I promise you. And if I do not have the document and I have the money, I’ll get you the document.
On paper, Mozambique has strict gun laws. Every buyer must register his gun for a license at a special police office in the Ministry of Interior. Stoltz tells me how to get around this.
Johan: Look, I haven’t taken my guns to the Ministry of the Interior, I just send my guy there, and he, just goes and applies for my, for my license.
(flash)
Mine takes 2 hours – some people’s takes 3 weeks. Depends how much DHL fees you pay.
Kathi: What is a DHL?
JOHAN: A DHL fee is courier services – it just goes quicker.
Time for the final blow. I let Stoltz know I’ve traced guns recovered from rhino crime scenes back to Investcon.
Johan: That was stolen! All my CZs is in my safe.
Kathi: Oh, really...really?
Johan: yes!
(flash)
Johan: “How the hell does that happen? So I only have 7 rifles, or 6 rifles…”
Far from 6 or 7, my paper trail shows Investcon has over 120 guns. Johan then blames the Ministry of Interior.
Johan: “It must be people that is working inside there.”
The link as to how the guns get to poaching operations still eludes me, until Stoltz leads me directly to “his guy.”
Kathi: “Was there ever any police officer that you worked with directly? There has to be someone you know.”
Johan: “Yah, there is a guy that I you, work with.” (white flash) He’s now based in Magude. He’s just the one who’s always doing my licenses for me. l would not be then surprised, if my guy in Magude does have maybe a finger in the pie.”
Stoltz is connected to some big people in the government and police. His partner in Investcon is Eugenio Numaio, the former governor of Gaza Province, which is next to Kruger’s border where all the poaching villages are located. And his guy? Officer Joaquim Maholele a top policeman in the key poaching town of Magude.
UPSOUND: I’M SUPPOSED TO CALL MAHOLELE AND LET HIM KNOW THAT I’M ON MY WAY. IF IT’S A TRAP, IT’S DANGEROUS, WE’LL GO BACK TO MAPUTO.
UPSOUND: “I’m Maholele.”
I go inside the police station with an undercover police ally disguised as a translator. Officer Maholele tells us his side of the story.
Maulele: If the rifles’ appearing, I’m the responsibility. I’m the one, the one to make all the license for Limnetzi Safari.
(flash)
When [Johan] buy the weapons, he call me. It’s the contract me and him. When he send me to go to Ministry to take the license, and with the license I’m going to the shops there, to pick up.
Kathi: And did you pick them, those weapons up from which, which gun shop?
Maulele: Afrocaça F
Kathi: Afrocaca, what about Casa Fabiao?
Maulele: Yeah, some Casa Fabiao.
My translator repeats how Stoltz pays Officer Maholele to legitimize documents at the Ministry of Interior before bringing all the hunting rifles back with him to Gaza province.
TRANSLATOR: Asked him to go to the province of Gaza, to legalize what was illegal.
I corner Officer Maholele and insist he show me the original licenses...
Maholele: This is a problem. This is a fucking problem!
He says they’re hidden at home -- under his bed!
